newsitem.title: USA: Dock crash slows ammonia movement on river-trade.
newsitem.headline: Dock crash slows ammonia movement on river-trade.

text.p: Movement of ammonia on the Mississippi River has been slowed after a grain barge crashed into a loading dock at a Monsanto Comp. ammonia manufacturing facility in Luling, La. on Monday, cash sources said.
"They are going to have to make special arrangements to move their ammonia," said one market observer. "This is really going to snug up supplies of ammonia, at least temporarily."
A spokesman for Monsanto in St. Loius, Mo. said that that damage to the dock was still being assessed by plant officials, and it was expected to remain out of service for approximately one week.
"We will find alternative ways to ship the ammonia and the people at the plant don't expect any disruptions in delivery to our customers," said company spokesman Larry O'Neill.
O'Neill said he was unaware if the crash had caused any disruptions in ammonia barge traffic so far this week and did not know if the crash had slowed other barge traffic on the Mississippi.
The Luling facility has several docks on the Mississippi, but the only one damaged was the one used for loading barges with ammonia. The plant also manufactures herbicides, the spokesman said.
